takeaway: The research is now a proof-controlled money-movement system, not a broad theme memo.
evidence_basis: Named-cash requirements matrix, execution status matrix, and decisive source request packet define source, wrapper, destination, cash use, receipt/settlement, payback/legal availability, and return gates.
why_it_matters: Keeps the thesis disciplined and auditable.
current_boundary: No case yet clears every named-cash proof gate.
next_action: Use the proof gates as promotion rules for every future case.

takeaway: The core thesis is routing-specific: different wrappers require different proof.
evidence_basis: Private credit, regulated utility recovery, LNG/project finance, fleet ABL, insurance statutory capital, and refinancing lanes each have separate source families and pass tests.
why_it_matters: Prevents generic claims about private credit, capex, or infrastructure from replacing evidence.
current_boundary: The research cannot collapse all lanes into one denominator or one proof type.
next_action: Keep lane-specific source packages and do not rank incomparable proxy metrics together.

takeaway: FPL is the best public customer-receipt route, but still lacks named customer-cash proof.
evidence_basis: FPL public PSC route shows petition, program testimony, factor support, amended factor support, aggregate SPPCRC revenue, category cost/recovery proxy, discovery route, response notices, and audit route.
why_it_matters: Shows where regulated cost recovery can become cash proof if workpapers are acquired.
current_boundary: Missing billed/collected customer cash, category receipt allocation, source-of-funds allocation, legal-entity waterfall, and earned-return workpapers.
next_action: Acquire FPL discovery answers, POD productions, Form 4P/Form 5P workpapers, receipt ledgers, and earned-return support.

takeaway: Wheaton/BHP Antamina is the closest two-sided named transaction.
evidence_basis: Current evidence shows Wheaton paid 4.300B USD, BHP received 4.300B USD, BHP booked streaming arrangement liability, and delivery/cash-back mechanics are visible.
why_it_matters: This is the strongest named payer-recipient-asset bridge in the system.
current_boundary: Missing BHP use allocation, PMPA-only settlement ledger, lender waterfall, tax/interest allocation, reserve-backed IRR/NPV/payback.
next_action: Acquire PMPA-only delivery, invoice, settlement, lender, and return-model support.

takeaway: PBF is the cleanest transaction source/use proxy, not full refinancing-value proof.
evidence_basis: Public filings show new notes, net proceeds, completed old-note redemption, available-cash bridge, and derived accrued-interest proxy.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates how far SEC filings can carry refinancing proof before trustee/payor detail is needed.
current_boundary: Missing trustee settlement, paying-agent transfer, exact accrued interest, fee/tax treatment, ABL availability, after-tax NPV, and refinery-level return.
next_action: Acquire redemption settlement, paying-agent confirmation, fee/tax model, ABL support, and pro forma debt-service/NPV model.

takeaway: URI is the best collateral/fleet-cash proxy but lacks certificate-grade proof.
evidence_basis: URI evidence shows ABL mechanics, certificate-delivery condition, collateral route, fleet assets, rental revenue, OCF/capex coverage, and ROIC proxy.
why_it_matters: Shows capital converting into reusable fleet assets and cash-flow proxy.
current_boundary: Missing populated borrowing-base certificate, eligible collateral, NOLV, reserves, L/C deductions, and fleet-class lifecycle return.
next_action: Acquire borrowing-base certificate, availability report, eligible-collateral schedule, and fleet-class return model.

takeaway: Ares/Frontline is a strong borrower-facility marker but not borrower cash proof.
evidence_basis: Evidence shows Frontline operating borrower, Bain sponsor, Ares arranger/bookrunner role, first-lien markers, holder fair value, and commitments.
why_it_matters: Shows private credit reaches named operating borrowers, not only platform AUM.
current_boundary: Missing credit agreement, lender allocation, closing funds-flow, collateral package, borrower financials, repayment, and payoff route.
next_action: Acquire borrower credit agreement, lender schedule, funds-flow memo, collateral documents, and borrower cash schedules.

takeaway: Cheniere has strong physical output and entity mechanics, but not train-level cash proof.
evidence_basis: Evidence shows cargo/output reconciliation, contracted demand, entity debt, DSCR mechanics, and project route.
why_it_matters: Shows energy infrastructure has real operating-output evidence beyond capex narrative.
current_boundary: Missing train-level customer receipts, SPA invoice cash, restricted-account balances, actual DSCR, project EBITDA/DCF, and return.
next_action: Acquire trustee reports, DSCR certificates, SPA billing attribution, and project EBITDA/DCF support.

takeaway: Insurance capital remains high-value but needs statutory legal-entity schedules.
evidence_basis: Apollo/Athene and KKR/Global Atlantic evidence shows liability, invested-asset, asset-income, credit, and FHLB/collateral proxies plus statutory route maps.
why_it_matters: Insurance is likely important to the capital-flow thesis, but public-company aggregates are too high-level.
current_boundary: Missing Schedule D/BA holdings, NAIC designations, legal-entity investment income, impairments, liability-cost spread, and borrower allocation.
next_action: Acquire statutory annual statements, Schedule D/BA extracts, investment-income schedules, and spread workpapers.

takeaway: The repeated blockers are documents that reconcile cash, not more narrative sources.
evidence_basis: Recurring gaps are receipts, billing, settlement ledgers, debt waterfalls, legal-entity schedules, collateral certificates, source-to-use ledgers, project cash contribution, and return models.
why_it_matters: This identifies why many public sources are useful but insufficient.
current_boundary: Search and extraction should not keep re-querying sources that only return metadata, aggregate values, or notices.
next_action: Run targeted source acquisition by missing document family.

takeaway: The 519-company system is a funnel, not empirical proof across 519 companies.
evidence_basis: The universe template, pilot batch, source-visible rows, and queue artifacts classify companies by lane and next source need.
why_it_matters: Lets the research scale without pretending every row is proven.
current_boundary: Queued or source-visible status is not full proof or representative universe evidence.
next_action: Use the universe to prioritize extraction and keep non-proven rows explicitly queued or bounded.

takeaway: The final safe conclusion is strong but bounded: map proven, full cash loop unproven.
evidence_basis: The current system can identify strongest candidates, visible money paths, cash/proxy evidence, proof gaps, and request-grade source packages.
why_it_matters: This is the right stopping point for the current sprint and the right launch point for source acquisition.
current_boundary: No named case has full source-use-receipt-payback-return proof.
next_action: Start with FPL records/POD workpapers, then Wheaton/PBF lender/trustee packages, then URI certificates and insurance statutory schedules.
